comment: Zoning ordinance numbers not referenced on cover sheet. The cover sheet shows Zoning Case No. C14-2013-0093 and Zoning MF-2 but does not display the actual applicable zoning ordinance numbers (such as Ordinance No. 20120112-092). Both the zoning case number AND the ordinance numbers must be shown.

Zoning conditions or restrictions not listed on cover sheet. The property is subject to Residential Design Standards (Subchapter F) compatibility standards triggered by the adjacent SF-3 parcel to the south, which limit structures within 25 feet of the SF-3 lot line to a maximum of 2 stories and 30 feet in height. These zoning conditions must be noted on the cover sheet.

Surveyor's company name, address, and telephone number not shown on cover sheet. The Surveyor role is entirely missing from the Site Development Data table. The surveyor's firm name, contact address, and phone number must be added to the table.
applicableAreas: Cover sheet - Site Development Data table

comment: Required legal instruments not listed on cover sheet. A consolidated 'Legal Instruments' section listing all easements, restrictive covenants, maintenance agreements, and other legal encumbrances affecting the property is missing. The property is encumbered by recorded easements including a Greenbelt Access & Use Easement (Instrument 2010070731) and a City of Austin Drainage Easement (Instrument 2011021137), among others, which must be documented on the cover sheet.

Maintenance agreement document number not referenced on cover sheet. The cover sheet states 'The proposed stacked biofiltration/detention pond will be privately maintained' but does not provide a recorded maintenance agreement document number or a placeholder for one. For a multi-family development with a water quality detention/biofiltration pond, a formal maintenance agreement referenced by recorded document number is required. Include a note in the format: 'Maintenance Agreement for [Facility Name] filed in document No. ________, Official Public Records, Travis County, Texas' with a blank placeholder if not yet recorded.

The Site Plan Approval block on the cover sheet fails to identify the site's development zone classification. Per facts.md, the site is located within the West Bouldin Creek watershed (Urban classification, non-water-supply), which places it within the Desired Development Zone (DDZ). The approval block must explicitly state "DDZ" to satisfy code requirements.

Multiple non-cover plan sheets lack the required blank batch stamp space in the lower right corner. Sheets 2, 9, 11, and 12 show engineer seals, title blocks, and project tracking information occupying the lower right corner instead of reserving a minimum 3.5"×5" blank space (or alternative 1"×1") for City of Austin batch stamping. All non-cover sheets must reserve this space in the lower right corner and may not include full approval blocks.

The Site Plan Approval block includes the text "RELEASED FOR GENERAL COMPLIANCE," which must be removed. This language is not compatible with formal site plan approval blocks and conflicts with development services procedures.

The Austin Fire Department signature line text reads "City of Austin Fire Department" instead of the required "Austin Fire Department." The signature line must be corrected to read "Austin Fire Department" to match standard departmental naming conventions.

The case manager name "Jim Gobel" appears in the approval block, but cannot be verified from submitted plan documents as the currently assigned case manager for this project. The case manager assignment must be confirmed against the current DSD case management system to ensure accuracy.

The presence or absence of force main components in the utility plans cannot be determined from available documents. If force main components are present, the "Austin Water Facility Engineering" signature line with a Date field must appear on both the cover sheet and each sheet containing force main components. The utility plan sheets must be reviewed to verify whether this signature line is required.
applicableAreas: Cover sheet and utility plan sheets

comment: The sheet index on the cover sheet lists Sheet 2 as 'Notes,' but the actual sheet is titled 'Plat.' The sheet index entry does not match the title block on the individual sheet. Please correct the cover sheet index to show the accurate title 'Plat' for Sheet 2.

The landscape sheets (prepared by Blu Fish Collaborative) show an incorrect total sheet count in the 'Y' position of the 'X of Y' format. These sheets are numbered as part of a 35-sheet set (e.g., '27 of 35', '28 of 35', '33 of 35', '34 of 35') rather than the 39-sheet set indicated on the cover sheet approval block and sheet index. All sheets in the plan set must display the consistent and accurate total count of 39 in the lower right corner.

The landscape sheets are not integrated into the plan set's overall sequential whole-number numbering system. They are numbered as part of a separate 35-sheet set rather than the combined 39-sheet plan set. Landscape sheets must be renumbered to be sequential with the full plan set (e.g., sheets 30-37 should be properly identified with their actual position in the overall 39-sheet sequence with 'X of 39' notation).

Building finished floor elevations are inconsistent across sheets: Building 1 shown as FFE 687.50 on Sheet 29 but 688.50 on Sheet 30 (0.50-ft difference); Building 3 shown as FFE 685.50 on Sheet 29 but 688.0 on Sheet 30 (2.50-ft difference). Conflicts must be reconciled and authoritative sheet identified.

Sheet 30 contains a cross-reference note stating 'REFER SHEET 28 FOR TREE LIST,' but Sheet 28 contains Construction Details 7 (storm drain manholes and catch basins). The Tree List is located on Sheet 32. Incorrect sheet number must be corrected to reference Sheet 32.

Sheet 23 contains duplicate fire hydrant installation notes appearing in both Block 7 and Block 9, with identical content. Duplicate construction details must be consolidated into a single authoritative instance and removed from secondary locations.

Condominium-specific requirement note (Chapter 81/82 Property Code compliance) is present on Sheet 9, Block 5, item (g). Applicability cannot be verified without confirmation of the project's actual legal structure (whether it will be filed as a condominium or as multi-family rental). The applicant's intent and housing/condominium documentation must be reviewed to determine if this note is appropriately applicable.
applicableAreas: Site Plan Release Notes on Sheet 9

comment: Fire Zone Notes, Item 1 references 'lockers and boat slip retaining walls' which are not applicable to this residential townhomes development. This boilerplate language must be removed or replaced with site-specific requirements. The note currently reads: 'Restricted Zone signage to be placed on front of lockers and along boat slip retaining walls as necessary or required.'
applicableAreas: Fire Zone Notes on Fire Protection Plan

comment: Recycling ordinance note (Block 11, Sheet 1) references the outdated 'Commercial and Multi-Family Recycling Ordinance.' Per current City of Austin standards, this must be updated to reference the 'Universal Recycling Ordinance' to reflect the current regulatory language.

Austin Fire Department requirements table (Block 5, Sheet 1) cites the '2021 International Fire Code Edition.' This must be updated to the 2024 International Fire Code to reflect the current adopted edition per City of Austin local amendments.
applicableAreas: Fire Department requirements table on cover sheet

comment: Site Plan Release Notes, item (e) contains bracketed instructional template text that has not been replaced with project-specific information: '[or identify the service provider if other than the City of Austin].' This placeholder text must be removed and replaced with the actual utility service provider name (City of Austin Water and Wastewater Utility).
applicableAreas: Site Plan Release Notes on Sheet 9

comment: Integrated Pest Management Plan note (Block 12, Sheet 1) contains a blank placeholder for the recorded document number: 'document No.____________'. This placeholder must be replaced with the actual recorded document number once the IPM Plan agreement is filed in the Official Public Records of Travis County, Texas.

The Additional Review Acknowledgement section on the Austin Water General Information and Construction Notes Sheet is incomplete. The section is missing critical fields required by UCM 2.5.1.E.22: the AMOC (Alternative Method of Compliance) field with approval number and date, and a formal OWRS (Onsite Water Reuse System) Acknowledgment Form section. The current form shows only AULCC, ONSITE WATER REUSE & AW RECLAIMED INFORMATION questions, AUTOMATED METERING INFORMATION, and AULCC fields, but lacks the AMOC documentation field and complete OWRS acknowledgment fields that must be present in the current AW template.
applicableAreas: Austin Water General Information and Construction Notes Sheet

comment: The owner is WM 41 Austin RE, LLC, a legal entity. Richard D. Agnew signed as 'Authorized Signer' on the application, but no corporate resolution, operating agreement extract, or other documentation demonstrating his legal authority to bind the LLC is provided in the submittal package. When a corporation, partnership, LLC, trust, or other legal entity executes an application, proof of the signatory's authority is required.

The applicant (Jason Rodgers, P.E., Bleyl Engineering) is not the property owner (WM 41 Austin RE, LLC). While the owner has signed on page 3 of the application, no separate written authorization letter from the owner of record specifically authorizing the applicant to submit and represent the property owner in this application is provided.

The owner is a legal entity: WM 41 Austin RE, LLC. The application shows Richard D. Agnew signed as 'Authorized Signer,' but the signatory's title and authorization to bind the entity are not documented. No corporate resolution, operating agreement extract, or other instrument demonstrating legal authority is included in the submittal package.

No warranty deed establishing current ownership of the subject property (Lot 1 Mecey Subdivision, 2.16 acres) has been provided in the submittal package. A current warranty deed is required to establish and confirm legal title and ownership status.

An Affidavit of No Liens is not provided in the submittal package. This document must be formally notarized with notary signature, official seal, and acknowledgment date, and must be signed by the record owner or authorized agent.

An Ownership and Lien Search Certificate from a third-party title company is not provided in the submittal package. This certificate must be current within 30 days of submittal to verify the property's lien status.

Landscape plan shows proposed paving (H.1) and other landscape features (H.2-H.7) but does not clearly establish a legend that explicitly distinguishes parking/circulation surfaces from buildings and vegetation areas per FPCM requirements. While hatch patterns differentiate zones, the legend does not clearly isolate hard surface types for parking versus other hard surfaces.

Landscape plan shows planting zones and identifies areas for parking lot landscaping (H.4) and street yard plantings (H.2, H.3) but does not provide specific dimensions (size and height) for individual proposed planters.

Building heights are documented in the Building Height Table (Sheet 9, ranging 33'-4.75" to 36'-1"), and fire apparatus clearance (14 feet) is noted as a general requirement on Sheet 3. However, specific building overhang dimensions are not explicitly shown on the site plan to allow canopy conflict assessment.

The existing demolished structure (slab FFE 686.8') is shown on the demolition plan but is not dimensioned with overall length and width measurements. Only the finished floor elevation is provided; structural footprint dimensions are absent.

A Tree Legend is provided (Block 6, Sheet 8) distinguishing trees to remain, heritage trees, protected trees, and trees to be removed. However, no comprehensive legend is provided for structural demolition items (concrete, asphalt, utilities, etc.). Demolition items are identified by individual text callouts rather than a standardized symbol/legend system for structures and improvements to be removed.

Sheet 8 contains Site Demolition Notes (Block 5) providing procedural instructions for tree protection, utility abandonment, and general demolition activities. However, no clear scope statement distinguishes what demolition work is included in this site plan versus work covered by separate demolition permits or other related projects.

The existing structure (assisted living facility foundation slab) is shown for demolition but lacks detailed demolition callouts specifying demolition methodology. Site demolition notes reference hand-tool requirements for tree protection but do not address specific methodology for removal of the complex structure itself.

General release notes (Sheet 3, Block 12) state 'All improvements shall be made in accordance with the released site plan' and reference demolition permits separately. However, no comprehensive statement clearly identifies which specific improvements are included in this site plan versus improvements proposed under separate permits, construction plans, or related projects.
applicableAreas: Cover Sheet (Sheet 1), General Notes (Sheet 3), Site Plan (Sheet 9)

comment: Project scope (39 townhome units, 8 buildings) is embedded in the cover sheet data and site plan details but no dedicated 'Scope of Work' statement block clearly details the proposed site work, improvements, and construction activities in a comprehensive narrative format.

The project includes eight multi-family residential buildings (vertical construction) shown on the site plan. No dedicated Construction Plan (C Plan) sheet providing detailed vertical construction information appears in the 39-sheet site plan package. Sheets 22-28 are labeled 'Construction Details' but address utility infrastructure details, not vertical/building construction. It is unclear whether a C Plan must be part of the site plan submittal or is submitted separately with building permit applications.

Existing and proposed land uses are not shown on the cover sheet. The cover sheet identifies the project as 'Valley View Townhomes' and indicates R3 occupancy classification, but does not provide a summary listing existing conditions versus proposed multi-family residential use.

The overall site plan sheet is too congested to show adequate detail at required scale. The single sheet attempts to display the site plan drawing with all buildings, utilities, and infrastructure along with five data tables, eight text note blocks, benchmark data, and detailed lighting figures, resulting in highly dense visual presentation with minimal white space. Information should be distributed across multiple sheets to ensure clarity and legibility at the required scale.

No dedicated paving plan sheet submitted with the site plan. Paving details and specifications are distributed across the Landscape Plan (Sheet 31) and Construction Details sheets (Sheets 22-28), rather than being consolidated on a single paving plan sheet as required.

Legends are not shown on the site plan sheet itself. While legends are provided on Sheet 3 (General Notes) and Sheet 11 (Grading Plan), Sheet 9 (the primary Site Plan) lacks a legend defining line types, symbols, colors, and hatching patterns used to distinguish features on that drawing.
applicableAreas: Site plan sheet and grading/dimension control sheets

comment: Vicinity plan not provided showing the class of every building/structure in the vicinity of the project site. The site location map on the cover sheet identifies surrounding parcels and streets but does not classify the buildings or structures in the vicinity.

Figure 2.5.1 (site regulations) required as a legible copy with the site plan application cannot be verified as present in the submitted plan set. No reference to Figure 2.5.1 was found in the sheet guides or content documentation.

Demolition plan sheet does not include an overlay of the current/proposed site plan to provide spatial context for what is being removed. Sheet 8 shows existing conditions with demolition callouts but does not overlay the proposed site plan footprints and building locations, making it difficult to understand how the demolition relates to the final proposed development.

Property boundary lines are shown on site plan, grading plan, ESC plan, utility plan, and addressing plan, but are absent from the landscape plan. Property boundaries must appear on all applicable civil plan sheets per UCM 2.5.1.E.9.

The legend defines general "Existing Easement" and "Easement (PUE)" symbols but does not explicitly define a specific linetype for drainage easements. LDC § 25-7-33(D)(3) requires distinct linetype definitions for drainage easements in the plan legend.

Right-of-Way (ROW) boundary symbol is not included in the plan legend on Sheet 3. While the ROW is labeled as text ("Valley View Road 50' R.O.W.") on plan sheets, the ROW boundary linetype must be defined in the legend.

Floodplain line types in the legend show only "100 yr" without distinction between City of Austin 100-year floodplain and FEMA floodplain. LDC § 25-7-33(D)(3) requires that the City of Austin 100-year floodplain and FEMA floodplain be shown separately on plan sheets with distinct linetypes defined in the legend.

Drainage easements recorded on the Cortez Heights plat (Vol 64/13, C8-71-079) and Trico Subdivision plat (Vol 69/14, C8S-74-075) are not properly depicted with complete recording instrument numbers on the plan sheets. The 25' Drainage Easement and 7.5' PUE from Vol 64/13 and the 10' Drainage Easement from Vol 69/14 identified in the property records are not verified on the submitted site plan. LDC § 25-7-33(D)(3) requires all recorded drainage easements to be depicted as delineated linework.

Street addresses are not labeled on building structures on the site plan or addressing plan. Only building numbers (Bldg. 1-8) and unit numbers (Unit 101-806) are shown. Per UCM 2.5.1.E.14, the street address for all structures must appear on the lot(s) where the structures are located on utility plan sheets.

Building use or function (Multi-Family Residential) is not labeled directly on building footprints on the site plan. Use information appears only in data tables on the plan sheet, not as direct labels on structures. Per BCM 1.2.7, site plan must show building location and size with use identification.

Existing versus proposed status is not labeled consistently. Existing adjacent buildings are labeled "Existing Apartment Building," but proposed buildings (Bldg. 1-8) are not labeled "Proposed" - only identified by building numbers. UCM 2.5.1.E.11 requires consistent labeling of existing versus proposed improvements.

Unit types (Two-Bedroom and Three-Bedroom) are not labeled on the site plan for multi-family residential buildings. Only unit numbers (Unit 101-806) are shown; unit types are not identified on the plans. Per City of Austin Addressing Standards, unit types must be labeled on site plan for multi-family residential projects.

LOC (Land Area Calculation) number is not included in the Site Data Table. The site plan shows Limits of Construction of 2.26 acres on the cover sheet (Sheet 1), but this value and the corresponding LOC number must appear in the SDT to confirm ICR applicability.

The Limits of Construction (2.26 acres, shown on cover sheet) differs from the Site Area on the SDT (2.162 acres). A separate table showing the total area within the limits of construction must be provided on the overall site plan sheet for clarity on which area applies to which calculations.

Widths of vehicular access points are not shown in the Site Data Table. Although access point widths are depicted on the site plan drawing (22.5' for Type II driveway and 26.0' for Type III driveway), these dimensions must be included in the SDT for comprehensive site data documentation.

Minimum site area required per MF-2 zoning is not shown in the Site Data Table. Although a separate Site Area Calculation table (Block 17) shows the requirement of 93,600 sf for 39 2+ bedroom units, this required value must appear in the SDT for direct comparison with the provided site area of 94,192 sf.

Gross floor area is not shown for each individual building separately in the Site Data Table. Although a separate Building Data Table (Block 15) shows GFA by building (ranging from 8,550 sf to 13,004 sf), these individual values must be included in the SDT for compliance documentation.

GFA calculation cannot be verified as correct without access to detailed building floor plans showing clear heights, loading dock areas, atrium spaces, parking, enclosed loading berths, and off-street maneuvering areas. The total GFA of 83,986 sf is shown in the SDT, but its compliance with the LDC § 25-1-21(47) definition cannot be assessed from the available site plan documents.

Building coverage calculation cannot be verified without detailed building plans showing footprints, projecting eaves, balconies, and other features to confirm they were properly excluded from the 32,296 sf (34%) proposed building coverage figure per LDC § 25-1-21(14).

Impervious cover calculation worksheets (Q1/Q2 tables or detailed IC calculation showing component breakdown) are not provided in the available documents. Without access to the detailed impervious cover calculation worksheet, compliance with the requirement that the 2-foot projection exemption not be applied to site plans cannot be verified.
Floor-to-area ratio (FAR) is not shown in the Site Data Table. The SDT must display FAR expressed as a ratio (e.g., 0.55:1) for the proposed development.
Both proposed FAR and maximum allowed FAR are not shown in the Site Data Table. For MF-2 zoning, the maximum FAR per LDC § 25-2-492 is 1:1; the SDT must show this maximum alongside the proposed FAR.

Open space is not shown in the Site Data Table in both square feet and percentage. The SDT lists Common Open Space Required as 4709.62 sf and Provided as 4710 sf, but the percentage of site area is not shown.

Building height is not shown in the Site Data Table in both stories and feet. Although a separate Building Height Table (Block 14) exists on Sheet 9, the maximum building height must be documented in the SDT; the heights range from 33'-4.75" to 36'-1", all under the 40' limit.

Both proposed building height and maximum allowed building height are not shown in the Site Data Table. The SDT must include the maximum allowed height (40' for MF-2) and the proposed maximum height (36'-1") for compliance comparison.

Finished floor elevation (FFE) is not documented per building in the Site Data Table. Although FFE values are labeled on the grading plan drawing (Sheet 11), they must appear in the SDT in feet above sea level per FPCM requirements: Building 1 (687.50'), Building 2-4 and 8 (685.50'), Building 5-6 (683.00'), Building 7 (685.00').

Maximum elevation permitted by zoning is not shown alongside proposed FFE in the Site Data Table. Since FFE is not in the SDT, this compliance comparison cannot be made. The SDT must show both proposed FFE and the maximum permissible elevation based on the zoning height limit and grade baseline.

The Site Data Table does not show both proposed and maximum allowed values for all applicable fields. Missing comparisons include: FAR (not shown at all), building height (not in SDT), FFE (not in SDT), and Gross Floor Area maximum (not applicable to show max). The SDT must document all development standards with their allowed and proposed values in side-by-side comparison format.

FAR is not expressed as a ratio in X:1 format on any site plan sheet. FAR is not shown on the cover sheet or the site plan (Sheet 9). Applicant must calculate and display FAR as a ratio (GFA ÷ Gross Site Area = approximately 0.891:1 for this project) on the site data table.

FAR calculation is not demonstrated. The work showing GFA divided by Gross Site Area is not presented anywhere on the plans. Applicant must add a calculation line to the Site Data Table showing FAR as GFA / Gross Site Area in X:1 ratio format.

FAR values cannot be compared across multiple locations because FAR is not shown on the cover sheet, site plan, or in publicly available excerpts from the benchmarking application. Per master comment OWB2, FAR consistency between the site data table and benchmarking application is a pending item that applicant has not yet resolved.

Unit type breakdown table in the requested format is not provided. The project shows 16 Two Bedroom and 23 Three Bedroom units in an aggregate summary, but does not provide a standalone table with columns for studio/efficiency, 1 bedroom, 2 bedroom, and 3 bedroom unit counts. Per Site Plan Review comment SP1, applicant must add a separate table showing unit counts by bedroom type.

Bedroom count per unit type cannot be verified from the available site plan documentation. While the project shows 16 Two Bedroom units and 23 Three Bedroom units at the project summary level, architectural floor plans showing individual unit bedroom configurations are not included in the primary site plan set. Unit type details must be shown in floor plans or a detailed building schedule.

Gross floor area of 83,986 sf on a 94,192 sf site yields a Floor Area Ratio of 0.89:1, exceeding the maximum FAR of 0.5:1 allowed for MF-2 zoning per LDC § 25-2-492. No variance, bonus, or exemption documentation is provided. Reduce building mass or obtain an approved FAR variance prior to site plan approval.

Site Data Table lists the proposed use as 'Multi-Family Residential' (with hyphen), but the correct LDC-defined term per § 25-2-3 is 'Multifamily Residential' (no hyphen, one word for 'Multifamily'). Update to use the exact LDC-defined terminology.

Parking summary table lists the land use as 'Residential', which is a generic term. Per LDC Chapter 25-6, Appendix A, parking tables must use the exact use name category (e.g., 'Residential Dwelling Units' or the specific category defined in Appendix A for multifamily residential uses). Update parking table with the specific use category from Appendix A.

Site Data Table shows 'Multi-Family Residential' but the correct LDC-defined sub-type per § 25-2-3 must be specified as 'Multifamily Residential', 'Condominium Residential', or 'Townhouse Residential'. Update to the correct LDC term formatted as written in § 25-2-3 (one word for 'Multifamily', no hyphen).

Adjacent property uses are labeled generically or incompletely: north and east show 'Existing Apartment Building' instead of the specific LDC classification (either 'Multifamily Residential' or 'Condominium Residential'); south shows '(Single-Family)' instead of 'Single Family Residential'. Update all adjacent property labels on the site plan to use specific LDC-defined use classifications per §§ 25-2-3 through 25-2-6.
applicableAreas: Site plan adjacent property labels - north, east, and south boundaries

comment: No building elevation drawings are included in the bound plan set (39 sheets). Building height information is provided only in tabular form on Sheet 9 (Building Height Table) and Sheet 29 (Finished Floor Elevations). Architectural elevation sheets must be included in the bound plan set and referenced in the Index of Sheets.

Elevation sheets are not provided for any of the 8 buildings. No elevation views are shown for any sides of any building. Provide separate architectural elevation sheets for each of the 8 distinct building types, showing all visible elevations from cardinal directions.

The project includes multiple distinct building types (4-Plex, 5-Plex, and 6-Plex) as shown in the Building Data Table on Sheet 9, but no separate architectural elevation sheets are provided for each building type. Provide distinct elevation sheets for each building type.

Building heights are shown in feet on the site plan data table (Sheet 9), but elevation sheets—which are the primary location for detailed height labeling—are not provided. Provide building elevation sheets with heights clearly labeled in feet from the average adjacent grade to the applicable roof point.

Building height is not labeled in number of stories on elevation sheets. While Sheet 9 notes 'Maximum Number of Building Stories = 3,' individual story counts are not labeled for each of the 8 buildings. Provide elevation sheets labeling the number of stories for each building.

Heights of individual buildings are shown in the Site Plan data table (Sheet 9) ranging from 33'-4.75" to 36'-1", with maximum height of 36'-1" (Building 3) identified, but no elevation sheets are provided where heights would be clearly separated by building. Provide architectural elevation sheets showing heights for each individual building.

Elevation sheets do not show the average adjacent grade (AAG) calculation. While the Building Height Table on Sheet 9 lists an 'Average (MSL)' value for each building (e.g., 686.25, 684.50, 685.00, etc.), it does not identify the highest and lowest grade points at the building perimeter or show the AAG calculation formula AAG = (highest + lowest) ÷ 2. The Grading Plan (Sheet 11) contains numerous spot elevations around buildings but lacks labeled AAG values and dimension lines from AAG to the roof point. Provide elevation sheets showing the highest and lowest grade points at each building perimeter (labeled 'AT BUILDING PERIMETER') and the vertical dimension from the calculated AAG to the applicable measurement point.

The Building Height Table on Sheet 9 does not specify the roof type for each building (flat, pitched, hip, mansard, or other), which is required to determine the correct height measurement methodology per LDC § 25-1-21(50). Different roof types require measurement to different points: flat roofs measure to the top of coping; pitched or hip roofs measure to the average height of the highest gable; mansard roofs measure to the deck line; other styles measure to the highest point. Provide elevation sheets identifying the roof type for each building and documenting that the correct measurement point was used for each roof type.

Building height values show discrepancies across plan documents. The Building Height Table on Sheet 9 shows 'Average (MSL)' values (e.g., Building 1: 686.25, Building 2: 684.50) that differ from the Finished Floor Elevations shown on Sheet 11 Grading Plan and Sheet 29 Addressing Plan (e.g., Building 1: FFE 687.50, Building 2: FFE 685.50). The difference between 'Average (MSL)' and FFE is not explained, creating confusion about which value represents the grade baseline for height measurement. Ensure all height values are consistent across elevation sheets, site plan data tables, grading plan, addressing plan, and project narrative, and reconcile any differences with clear notation of whether values represent AAG, FFE, or finished grade at specific locations.

Required zoning district setback lines are not shown, labeled, or dimensioned on the site plan, grading plan, or landscape plan for the northern, eastern, and southern property boundaries. Only the western boundary (Valley View Road) shows a labeled platted setback. All required yard setback lines for the MF-2 zoning district must be clearly drawn, labeled, and dimensioned on the site plan.

Compliance with zoning district setback distances cannot be verified because required setback lines are not shown with dimensions from property boundaries to buildings. No dimensions are provided on the site plan, grading plan, or landscape plan showing the distance from building faces to the northern, eastern, or southern property lines. Provide dimensioned setback lines for all property boundaries with required setback values clearly labeled.

Article 10 compatibility standards applicability has been incorrectly determined. The site is zoned MF-2, which is less restrictive than MF-4, and is located adjacent to an SF-3-zoned property. SF-3 is SF-5 or more restrictive and qualifies as a triggering property under § 25-2-1053. If the development is within 75 feet of this SF-3 property boundary, Article 10 compatibility standards apply. The applicant marked 'No' on the consolidated application for compatibility standards applicability, but this appears to be incorrect. Clarify whether the southern boundary is within 75 feet of the triggering property, and if so, prepare a compatibility analysis and revised plans demonstrating Article 10 compliance.
applicableAreas: Southern property boundary adjacent to SF-3 zoning

comment: If Article 10 compatibility is triggered (site within 75 ft of SF-3 triggering property), the required compatibility buffer is not shown at the correct width along the shared property line. The compatibility buffer must be 25 feet wide (or 15 feet if the development site is less than 75 feet wide measured from the shared triggering property line), shown as a landscaped zone complying with § 25-8-700 planting requirements, and extending along the full length of the property line shared with the triggering property. No such labeled and dimensioned buffer line appears on the site plan or landscape plan.
applicableAreas: Southern property boundary adjacent to SF-3 property

comment: Triggering property or properties are not clearly identified on the site plan compatibility sheets with all required information. While the site plan vision analysis identified adjacent zoning labels (SF-3 on south), there is no separate compatibility exhibit clearly labeling the triggering property with its zoning designation (SF-3) and dwelling unit count (required to confirm it qualifies as a triggering property under § 25-2-1053). Prepare a compatibility exhibit showing the triggering property location, zoning, and dwelling unit count, and clearly label it on all relevant plan sheets.

Separate compatibility exhibit is not provided or is incomplete. If Article 10 compatibility is triggered, the required standalone compatibility exhibit must show: property boundaries, on-site and off-site zoning boundaries (including all triggering properties and applicable combining districts), distances from triggering property boundary to existing and proposed structures, distances to surface improvements (parking, driveways, drainage features), and location of existing structures on triggering properties. This documentation is required to demonstrate compliance with § 25-2-1061 (height limits), § 25-2-1062 (buffer), and § 25-2-1063 (screening).

Transformer pad clearances cannot be verified. Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows transformer locations on the site, but no clearance dimensions or construction details are provided demonstrating compliance with Austin Energy Design Criteria 1.10.4. The criteria require specific minimum clearances based on building construction type (e.g., 12 feet to non-masonry buildings, 5 feet to brick/masonry). Provide a transformer pad detail sheet showing clearance dimensions to all adjacent buildings and structures with notation of building construction type to verify compliance.

Adjoining land uses not labeled on the main site plan for north and south adjacent properties. Sheet 9 shows zoning for north but does not indicate land use, and south property has no zoning or land use designation. Main site plan must document all adjacent uses on all four sides.

Land uses for properties across Valley View Road (west of the public right-of-way) are not documented on the site plan. Properties on the opposite side of the street should have their land uses identified and labeled.
Adjacent property zoning designation not shown on main site plan for south property. East and north adjacent zoning are labeled on Sheet 9, but south property has no zoning designation displayed.

Discrepancy exists between sheet documentation: Sheet 9 shows north zoning as MF-4-CO while Sheet 11 shows MF-2-CO. Cannot verify accuracy against City GIS records. Confirm correct zoning designation.

Building footprints on adjoining properties within 50 feet are not clearly confirmed on main site plan for north and south sides. East side footprints are shown, but north and south adjacent building footprints are not clearly depicted on Sheet 9.

Verification note absent stating whether buildings exist on adjoining lots within 50 feet. Site plan must include note for each side where no buildings exist stating 'no buildings exist on adjoining lots within 50 feet.'

Documentation does not explicitly restrict exterior lighting above the second floor when facing or adjacent to residential properties. Provide note or detail confirming above-2nd-floor lighting restriction for locations adjacent to residential uses.
